facts.statement: The Farpoint mission closed at 41174.2: Farpoint Station was a captive spaceborne being, which was freed and left Deneb IV with its mate; Q let his trial of humanity stand and withdrew.

During the Farpoint mission the saucer was separated at about warp 9.5, past the red line, while fleeing Q; at Deneb IV the first officer docked the saucer manually from the battle bridge on the captain's order.

Engineering strain logs record that saucer docking latch four carried about half again its rated load for 0.4 seconds during the Farpoint separation; the other eleven latches stayed within rating; at the Deneb IV docking all twelve recorded seated and nominal.

Latch four's actuator housing has a fatigue crack about 11 mm long. The latch's internal sensors cannot detect it. About 3 mm of it reaches the housing's outer face, inside the ventral interface crawlway at frame 31, where it shows as a stress line to a structural scan at close range, or to La Forge's VISOR.

With the crack unrepaired, latch four releases normally in a controlled separation at sublight, and the crack grows a little each time. In an emergency separation at warp it jams; the separation completes only by tearing the latch from its housing, which breaches the ventral interface seal. The breach is contained by pressure doors and needs a starbase to repair.
A deep reading of latch four's Farpoint strain trace shows a ringing after the spike whose decay is consistent with a loss of stiffness in the housing; nobody has analysed the trace that way.
Starfleet's orders after Farpoint: begin the exploration survey of the sector beyond Deneb, the first leg at the captain's discretion, and file the full Farpoint report at the next relay.
facts.source: Starfleet orders, read at the Farpoint briefing

facts.statement: In the Ealat colony on Hesker IV, 31 people have fallen ill in 23 days with a fever followed by inflammation of the heart muscle; six have died, four of them children; nine are critical in the Javri infirmary, which has twelve beds.
Dr. Juuso's field lab found an RNA virus in patients' blood and stool that matches nothing in her human-pathogen database.
Juuso's case map: 27 of the 31 cases are in households of the four siidas grazing the Ninth, the colony's newest pasture, or at its summer camp.

The 2362 expansion report on the Ninth, written by Sara's council committee, says the soil survey found no deficiencies. Every sample was from the valley floor; the upland slopes where the herds graze were never sampled.

This spring, calves on the Ninth's upland slopes went stiff and could not stand, and about 400 died. Biret Eira reported it to the council; Sara told the council it was slope cramp from the steep ground.

The colony's founding survey of 2345, by the Federation Colonial Office, flagged the northern uplands as selenium-poor and recommended mineral supplements before any grazing there. Copies are in the council archive and in the Colonial Office's records.
Eira's herd is on the Ninth's eastern slopes with her brother Ante.

The pathogen is an Earth enterovirus that came with the colony's founding herds, which were shipped live from Earth by the founders' choice, not as genetic stock. It was harmless for nineteen years. In selenium-deficient animals on the Ninth's upland it mutated into a strain that inflames heart muscle, in calves and in people.

The herding cooperative's veterinary records, in its office at Javri, characterised the parent enterovirus in 2351 as a harmless gut virus of the herds. Nobody has compared them with Juuso's findings; the cooperative has had no vet since 2360.
The mutated strain stays virulent in animals and people whose selenium is normal. Supplementation prevents fresh mutation and eases the disease, but does not remove the strain.
facts.source: truth (real science: selenium-deficient hosts and viral virulence)

facts.statement: It spreads mainly by the faecal-oral route, through water, milk and handling. Reedflies carry it mechanically between herds on their mouthparts, a minor route.

Starfleet Medical relays the Ealat colony's request: an unidentified, possibly native pathogen causing fever and myocarditis on Hesker IV, 31 cases and 6 dead; the colony asks for medical assistance and cardiac support. Hesker IV is 4.1 light years from the Enterprise's position.

The Ninth's herds come down to the winter grounds when the first lasting snow closes the upland, and gather at the Javri corrals for the autumn separation, where all the colony's herds mix and the slaughter season begins.
The people of the Ninth's siidas eat meat and milk from the deficient herds and are low in selenium themselves, which worsens the disease in them.

MacDougal's required time for the latch inspection is about four hours: separation and stand-off half an hour; two suited teams of three inspecting the twelve housings at twenty minutes each, two hours; the redock approach from 500 m at 0.5 m/s, about seventeen minutes plus alignment; re-mating the interface and checks, an hour. Latch four alone would be about two and a half. Seven people on the hull, MacDougal included. The extra two hours in her six are for re-inspection if the imager shows something.

Yar's incident log: Q was aboard in person three times (on the bridge at the barrier, where he froze Lt. Torres; twice on the bridge near Deneb IV) and took the bridge crew to his courtroom. No intruder alert was sounded on any occasion, and no security team was dispatched. Eleven of the twenty-three security staff on watch learned an intruder was aboard only from the bridge feed on their posts' displays.

Data's comparison of the bridge optical record with the internal life-sign sensor logs, at standard settings and resolution, for Q's three in-person appearances on the bridge during the Farpoint mission: the optical record shows Q throughout; the internal sensors logged no life sign at his position in any interval, while every crew member present was logged normally. Scope: one ship's internal sensors at their routine settings; it does not establish that Q is undetectable by other means or settings.

La Forge's recollection, a day after, of Q as seen through his VISOR from the bridge's aft stations during the two in-person appearances near Deneb IV: a humanoid figure at an even temperature all over, face the same as hands, with no visible pulse and none of the small electrical flicker the VISOR usually shows in a living body. Scope: one observer's unrecorded memory of one instrument at a few metres; the VISOR does not record.

La Forge's recollection, on being asked: through his VISOR, Q's clothes, the judge's robes in the first Deneb IV appearance and the uniform in the second, read at the same even temperature as his face and hands. Scope: as F-043, one observer's unrecorded memory, recalled only when asked.
The survey plan's first stop is a red dwarf survey point 0.94 ly out from Deneb IV; at warp 5 the ship arrives about 2100 on day 2, with nine hours scheduled at sublight.
The captain's yeoman booked the first officer fourteen hundred today in the ready room, twenty minutes, for two items.
Lt. Torres, frozen by Q at the barrier, is cleared by sickbay for light duty and is on the roster at conn relief on beta shift from tomorrow.
The red dwarf at the first survey point is catalogued as a flare star of modest activity; its flares are the reason it is on the survey list.
facts.source: survey catalogue (decided at turn 15; red dwarfs commonly flare)

facts.statement: MacDougal's view of latch four: docked, it carries nothing it wasn't built for; the risk is the next separation, worst at warp in a hurry. She wants no planned separation until it is inspected, any emergency separation at sublight if there is a choice, and an inspection within about two weeks or at the next starbase, where drydock would do it without anyone outside.

MacDougal's interim restriction on latch four, in writing: no planned separation until inspected; any emergency separation at sublight wherever there is a choice; inspection within about two weeks or at the next starbase.

Data's records summary: Hesker IV, the Ealat colony, a Federation colony founded in 2345 by a herding cooperative from northern Earth; population about six thousand two hundred; main settlement Javri.
When Picard read out 'four of them children', Troi sensed from him a sharp grief, held down hard, out of proportion to the news; she will not say whose it was.
facts.source: Troi's empathic sense (a feeling, no facts)

facts.statement: Crew manifest search, qualifications outside sickbay: life sciences lab (under the second officer): Lt. (j.g.) Ilse Vantongeren, microbiologist, virus culture and sequencing; Ensign Kesi Mbatha, xenobiologist, Academy specialisation in comparative (animal) pathology; two biology lab technicians. Security: four field-medic certified, Ensign Abara among them. Civilians: one, Tomas Reyhan, a former emergency paramedic, now teaching at the ship's school; volunteers only. No physician and no qualified ICU nurse outside sickbay.

The Ealat colony's medical reports, as relayed by Starfleet Medical: 31 cases in 23 days; fever, then myocarditis; worst in children; six dead, four of them children; nine critical in a twelve-bed infirmary at Javri, with no cardiac support beyond drugs. In blood and stool, a small non-enveloped RNA virus about thirty nanometres across, matching nothing in the colony's medical database; no sequence data sent. Case map: 27 of 31 in households of the four herding groups on the colony's newest pasture, the Ninth. Dr. Juuso's assessment: a native pathogen, probably carried by a biting insect native to the Ninth's marshes, which the colonists call reedflies; the council is considering destroying their breeding grounds.

At the 1300 briefing: Crusher says viruses of that description spread on Earth mainly faecal-oral, through water, food and hands; insects can carry them only mechanically, on their bodies; so even if Juuso is right about the reedflies, destroying their breeding grounds would not stop it. Data adds that in the twentieth century poliovirus was recovered from houseflies, which were never shown to be the main route. Picard: no habitat destroyed on a hypothesis. Yar: the away team drinks and eats nothing local and touches nothing bare-handed.
The Ninth's summer camp draws its water from a stream below the slopes where the herds graze and cross; the herds wade it upstream of where the families fill their water.
facts.source: truth (decided at turn 23; consistent with F-030)

facts.statement: At the briefing: nobody aboard knows what the Ninth's families drink; the colony records don't say. Crusher's message to Juuso asks about water sources and advises boiling all water on the Ninth; the reply takes about forty minutes each way. MacDougal can have portable water purifiers replicated before arrival, about forty, limited by power cells. Crusher: children are both more exposed and, with viruses of this kind, more vulnerable.

At the briefing, Lt. (j.g.) Vantongeren (sequencing human samples) and Ens. Mbatha (sampling herds, water and wildlife on the Ninth) are reassigned to Dr. Crusher for Hesker IV, with Data's release (their stellar survey is suspended) and Picard's approval. Troi warns that strangers sampling the herds in the middle of this will look to herders like the first step to killing them.

At the briefing: Yar gives the medical effort three of her four field medics, not four, and wants to be asked first next time; Lloyd will ask Tomas Reyhan to volunteer; Picard will sign a request, drafted by Lloyd, for Starfleet Medical to send a physician and an ICU nurse after the ship, who will be days behind at best; Mbatha works with the herders, with their permission and their hands on their animals; Troi goes down for that.

Away team plan at the briefing: first wave on arrival: Lloyd, Crusher and two of her staff, Vantongeren, Mbatha, Troi, and Yar's quarantine team (Yar, two security, her one medic). Crusher's group to the Javri infirmary; Mbatha's group, with Troi, Yar's team and MacDougal's purifiers, to the Ninth. Full decon on every return; crew with symptoms to isolation in sickbay. Crusher wants the nine critical patients brought up for cardiac support; Picard rules that no patient comes aboard until Crusher has seen the virus under a microscope, and then he will decide.

End of the briefing: Lloyd goes to Javri, where the council meets; Yar's team covers the Ninth and she sends one security officer with Lloyd. Picard allows a cargo bay to be prepared as an isolation ward on its own environmental circuit, in case he decides to bring patients aboard; Crusher wants it at negative pressure with its own filtered air. Picard reminds Lloyd that in the council chamber he is a guest of the colony's government.

Picard on Lloyd's two items: he agrees to drydock at the nearest starbase after Hesker IV, or six hours at sublight in clear space, and wants Lloyd to find out which starbase and how far, to go to Starfleet with the Hesker report. He will read Yar's protocol before he signs anything, and wants to see Data's file on Q.
Picard has ordered La Forge's VISOR account of Q put into Data's Q file, all of it, in La Forge's own words.

La Forge: the VISOR keeps no record, not even a buffer; it is all live to his implants. A tap on the side of it could pick the signal off and send it to the ship to be recorded. Getting the signal out is the easy part; making the raw image mean anything to anyone but him is the hard part. Data wants to help build it.

MacDougal on the isolation ward: it can be done before Hesker IV. She estimates eighteen hours with her own people, twelve if the first officer lends her O'Brien and two from damage control for a shift; the bay has to be emptied first, which is ops' and the XO's business; she wants the bay nearest sickbay with its own environmental trunk; the purifiers come first for power cells, the ward first for people.
The request to Starfleet Medical for a physician and an ICU nurse to follow the Enterprise to Hesker IV, drafted by Lloyd, was signed by Picard and transmitted at 1347.
